docs.title: Chakra ConvAI
docs.text: Chakra ConvAI (chakra-convai, formerly chakra-ivr-core) is the licensed engine that runs a Chakra Labs conversational agent: on a phone line, as web voice with the user's camera, or as a typed chat. You write only what is specific to your service: what the agent says, the tools it can call, and a settings file. The engine runs the session.

docs.title: What the SDK Does vs. What You Provide
docs.text:
The SDK does this for you You provide this Answers calls through LiveKit and runs the whole call chakra.toml: your settings Speech in and out, on Chakra Voice or Gemini Live config/instructions.json: persona, rules, flows, and spoken lines Builds the system prompt from your configuration skills/: Python classes holding your tools Greets callers and remembers returning ones .env: your licence key and other secrets Handles silence, maximum call length, and daily talk-time limits data/: documents for the knowledge base (optional) Searches your knowledge base (RAG) hooks.py: custom behavior (optional) Records calls, feedback, and transcripts in your PostgreSQL database Database schema & migration logic Reports usage to the Chakra Console Business analytics

The package is delivered compiled, without Python source, and runs only with a valid licence key from Chakra Labs.

docs.title: From Chakra Labs
docs.text:
Item What it is Where it goes Install token Read-only access to the private package index FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN, at install and build time only Licence key Starts with chk_live_. Identifies your company and package CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY, at run time in .env Chakra Console sign-in An email and password for your company's dashboard Your web browser

Treat the install token and the licence key as secrets. Keep them in a secrets manager or CI secret store, never in source code.

docs.title: Your Own Infrastructure
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 on Linux x86_64: The package is built for this platform only. On Windows or macOS, develop inside Docker or WSL.
  • A LiveKit project: Connects your phone number or web app to the agent. You need its URL, API key, and API secret.
  • A Google API key: If you use the Gemini Live pipeline or the knowledge base (creates search embeddings).
  • A PostgreSQL database (optional, recommended): Without one the agent still takes calls, but caller memory, call records, and daily talk-time limits are off.

docs.title: Channels: Phone, Web Voice & Video, and Chat
docs.text:
chakra-convai supports three distinct channel modalities from a single shared codebase: 1. Phone (phone): Traditional telephony calls arriving through SIP trunks. 2. Web Voice & Video (web with mode: "voice"): Realtime voice streaming combined with user camera or screen sharing. 3. Web Chat (web with mode: "chat"): Low-latency typed text and photo messaging.

Each agent defined in chakra.toml declares its target channel ([[agents]] channel = "phone" | "web").

docs.title: Channel Comparison
docs.text: Feature Phone (phone) Web Voice (web_voice) Web Chat (web_chat) Transport SIP / Telephony trunk via LiveKit SIP LiveKit WebRTC Room LiveKit WebRTC Room User Input Spoken audio Audio + Camera / Screen Typed text + Photo uploads Agent Output Synthesized speech Synthesized speech Text responses Silence Handling Enabled (configurable check-ins) Enabled Disabled (uses idle timeout) Vision Support N/A Full (Gemini video / Chakra vision frames) Photos attached as user messages Talk Time Limits Enforced by daily caller limit Enforced by daily caller limit Excluded from talk limits Identity Keying Caller caller ID (phone number) user.phone or user.id user.phone or user.id

docs.title: 1. Phone Channel
docs.text:
Configured with channel = "phone". Phone sessions are dialed through SIP into LiveKit rooms. The caller ID becomes the user identity, linking directly to PostgreSQL caller memory and daily call duration limits.

[[agents]]
name = "phone_agent"
channel = "phone"
language = "si"

docs.title: 2. Web Voice & Video
docs.text:
Web voice sessions connect an end-user from an iOS, Android, or Web client via WebRTC.

[[agents]]
name = "web_voice_agent"
channel = "web"

docs.title: Multimodal Vision & Camera Frames
docs.text:
• gemini_live Pipeline: The agent natively subscribes to the user's incoming video track.
  • chakra Pipeline: The engine captures user camera frames ([web] vision_frames, default 4, one frame per second) and attaches them to each user speech turn. The managed LLM inspects what the user showed while speaking. Once a turn is complete, earlier frames are evicted so subsequent turns only bill their own tokens.

docs.title: 3. Web Chat
docs.text:
When an end-user interacts over chat (or when room name starts with chat_room_prefix), the session runs in text/photo mode:

[web]
chat_idle_timeout_seconds = 600
chat_model = "gemini-2.5-flash"
  • Spoken greetings, VAD, and silence detectors are disabled.
  • Image uploads from the user are converted into multimodal prompts.
  • Sessions automatically close when inactive after chat_idle_timeout_seconds.

docs.title: The Standard Session Data Format
docs.text:
Every web and mobile application sends session metadata inside the LiveKit room's metadata string:

{
  "chakra": {
    "version": 1,
    "mode": "voice",
    "language": "si",
    "user": {
      "id": "usr_99812",
      "phone": "0771234567",
      "name": "Nimal Perera"
    },
    "context": {
      "district": "Kandy",
      "crops": ["tomato", "chilli"],
      "account_tier": "premium"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Schema Details
docs.text:
• mode: "voice" or "chat".
  • language: ISO code ("si", "ta", "en") or descriptive language name. Locked for the session when [web] keep_language = true.
  • user: User identity fields. user.phone takes precedence for caller memory, falling back to user.id.
  • context: Arbitrary key-value dictionary that is formatted and injected directly into the LLM system prompt on every turn.

docs.title: Building Metadata in Python
docs.text:
Applications generating LiveKit room tokens in Python can use the built-in helper:

from chakra_convai import session_metadata

metadata_str = session_metadata(
    mode="voice",
    language="si",
    user_id="usr_99812",
    phone="0771234567",
    name="Nimal Perera",
    context={"district": "Kandy", "crops": ["tomato"]}
)

docs.title: CLI Commands Reference
docs.text:
chakra-convai provides a complete suite of commands for building, checking, testing, and running your voice agent application.

Run these commands from the root directory of your application (where chakra.toml, .env, and config/ reside).

docs.title: Command Summary
docs.text: Command Purpose License Required? chakra-convai init Bootstrap a new application boilerplate No (with --channels) chakra-convai check Validate configuration, skills, prompts, and license Yes chakra-convai console Talk to the agent directly in terminal Yes chakra-convai dev Run local worker with auto-reload Yes chakra-convai start Start production LiveKit worker Yes chakra-convai prompt [LANG] Print assembled system prompt for inspect/debug Yes chakra-convai build-rag Compile knowledge base vector index Yes chakra-convai kb <QUESTION> Query knowledge base from CLI Yes chakra-convai licence View active Chakra Console license details Yes chakra-convai download-files Pre-download model weights (Docker build step) No chakra-convai version Print engine version No

docs.title: chakra-convai init [DIR] [--name NAME] [--channels phone,web_voice,web_chat] [--force]
docs.text: Scaffolds a new application. - --channels: Comma-separated list of channels (phone, web_voice, web_chat). If omitted, queries Chakra Console using your CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY. - --force: Overwrite existing files.

docs.title: chakra-convai check
docs.text: Performs end-to-end static validation: - Resolves and verifies chakra.toml settings. - Discovers and validates all skills and @function_tool decorators. - Verifies that greeting, silence, and daily quota lines exist in config/instructions.json for all supported languages. - Verifies the cryptographic license against Chakra Console and ensures configured channels match the project type.

docs.title: chakra-convai console
docs.text: Launches an interactive voice terminal session using your microphone and speakers. Allows rapid prompt and skill testing without placing phone calls or opening a web app.

docs.title: chakra-convai dev
docs.text: Starts the worker process locally and monitors python source files, restarting worker instances on modification.

docs.title: chakra-convai start
docs.text: Runs the worker in production mode, listening for incoming LiveKit SIP dispatch jobs and web rooms.

docs.title: chakra-convai prompt [LANG]
docs.text: Prints the compiled system prompt that the model reads at runtime for the specified language (e.g. chakra-convai prompt si), including injected tool descriptions and guidelines.

docs.title: chakra-convai build-rag [--clean]
docs.text: Parses documents in data/, computes embeddings, and builds the Annoy index (data/rag.ann).

docs.title: chakra-convai kb <QUESTION> [LANG]
docs.text:
Tests knowledge retrieval directly from the terminal: 

chakra-convai kb "How do I identify fall armyworm?" en

docs.title: chakra-convai licence
docs.text: Queries Chakra Console and displays license metadata, allowed pipelines, channel permissions, and daily caller limits.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: The main configuration file for every application built on the engine is chakra.toml.

docs.title: Editor Autocompletion & Schema Validation
docs.text:
If you use VS Code (with the Even Better TOML extension), add this line at the top of chakra.toml for autocomplete and validation:

#:schema https://docs.chakralabs.ai/schema/chakra.json

docs.title: [app]
docs.text:
Global application properties:

[app]
name = "govi-mithuru"
skills = "govi_mithuru.skills"
hooks = "govi_mithuru.hooks"
default_language = "si"
supported_languages = ["si", "ta", "en"]
timezone = "Asia/Colombo"
config_dir = "config"
num_idle_processes = 2

docs.title: [[agents]]
docs.text:
Declares agents, their respective channels, and language bindings:

[[agents]]
name = "ivr_sinhala"
channel = "phone"
language = "si"

[[agents]]
name = "web_assistant"
channel = "web"

docs.title: [web]
docs.text:
Settings for web voice, video, and chat channels:

[web]
# Number of camera frames captured per user turn (1 frame/sec)
vision_frames = 4
# Enable vision frames on managed chakra pipeline
chakra_vision = true
# Gemini model for chat sessions on gemini_live licences
chat_model = "gemini-2.5-flash"
# Idle chat disconnect timeout in seconds
chat_idle_timeout_seconds = 600
# Preserve language selection throughout the web session
keep_language = true

docs.title: [pipeline]
docs.text:
Pipeline selection fallback:

[pipeline]
type = "chakra" # "chakra" or "gemini_live"

docs.title: [greeting]
docs.text:
Configures introductory lines spoken upon user connect:

[greeting]
first = "greetings.first_time"
returning_template = "greetings.returning"
returning_shape = "returning_caller"
delay_seconds = 0.5

docs.title: [features]
docs.text:
Enables optional engine subsystems:

[features]
database = true          # Connects to PostgreSQL for caller memory & analytics
transcripts = true       # Writes call turn transcripts to DB
memory_fallback = true   # Generates memory summary if caller hangs up abruptly

docs.title: [tools]
docs.text:
Registers built-in engine tools:

[tools]
builtin = [
  "end_call",
  "save_caller_memory",
  "capture_feedback",
  "query_knowledge_base"
]

docs.title: [silence]
docs.text:
Dictates user silence handling:

[silence]
mode = "monitor" # "monitor" (turn pipeline), "away" (Gemini Live), or "off"
timeout_seconds = 7.0
prompts = ["silence.check_in_1", "silence.check_in_2"]
goodbye = "silence.disconnect"

docs.title: [call] & [call_limit]
docs.text:
Call duration safety constraints and daily talk quotas:

[call]
max_duration_seconds = 900
caller_join_timeout_seconds = 20.0
max_duration_goodbye = "call.max_duration_reached"

[call_limit]
limit_reached = "limits.daily_limit_reached"
approaching_limit = "limits.warning"
time_up = "limits.goodbye"
min_usable_seconds = 30

docs.title: [rag] (Knowledge Base)
docs.text:
Vector retrieval configuration:

[rag]
top_n = 3
distance_threshold = 0.65
min_grounding = 0.2
show_sources = true

docs.title: Environment Variables (.env)
docs.text: Variable Description Required CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY Your cryptographic Chakra Console license key Yes LIVEKIT_URL LiveKit server WebSocket endpoint Yes LIVEKIT_API_KEY LiveKit project API key Yes LIVEKIT_API_SECRET LiveKit project API secret Yes GOOGLE_API_KEY Required for Gemini Live or RAG embedding creation Optional DATABASE_URL PostgreSQL connection string for caller memory and analytics Optional CHAKRA_PIPELINE Override default pipeline selection (chakra or gemini_live) Optional APP_PORT Port for the HTTP health / admin worker Optional LANGFUSE_* Tracing & observability credentials Optional

docs.title: Chakra Console Guide
docs.text: The Chakra Console is the web dashboard where your organization manages licenses, monitors usage, tunes talk-time limits, and customizes voice clones without code changes.

docs.title: First Sign-in
docs.text:
1. Open the Chakra Console address in your browser.
  2. Sign in with the organization email and initial password provided by Chakra Labs.
  3. Navigate to Account and update your password (at least 10 characters).

docs.title: 1. Dashboard
docs.text: The central overview of your organization's voice activity: - Usage Metrics: Total calls, aggregate minutes consumed, and average call duration for the current billing cycle. - Package Allowances: View your active monthly minute allowance, concurrency limits, and copy your CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY. - Pace & Projections: Forecasts expected month-end minute consumption based on recent calling volume. - Activity Visualizations: Interactive heatmaps of peak calling hours and daily usage charts.

docs.title: 2. Project View
docs.text: Each project represents a specific deployment (e.g., telephone helpline, web assistant): - View project type (phone, web_voice, web_chat). - Check active LiveKit room dispatches and per-agent pipeline allocations. - Monitor channel-specific consumption (voice minutes vs. chat token counts).

docs.title: 3. Talk-Time Limits
docs.text: Enforce daily allowances to prevent abuse and manage operational costs: - Per-Caller Tracking: Cumulative call duration is tracked against each caller's unique telephone number. - Midnight Resets: Quotas reset every night at midnight (Sri Lanka Time / Asia/Colombo). - Graceful Warning: Nearing callers hear a polite warning prompt before the session concludes. - Dynamic Propagation: Changes made in the Console take effect on running workers within 10 minutes without service restarts.

docs.title: 4. Voice Customization & Cloning
docs.text: Personalize the voice persona for your brand: - Preset Voices: Select from Chakra Labs' curated library of expressive voices. - Voice Cloning (Chakra Voice): 1. Upload a 5 to 10-second .wav audio clip of the target speaker recorded in a quiet environment. 2. Enter the exact transcript of the words spoken (e.g. in Sinhala). The transcript must match the spoken audio precisely. 3. The cloned voice propagates to your live agents within minutes. Existing calls preserve their starting voice to prevent mid-call disruption.

docs.title: Important Timings & Billing
docs.text:
• Monthly Reset: Usage quotas reset on the 1st of every calendar month (Sri Lanka time).
  • Dashboard Refresh: Telemetry updates in the Console approximately every 2 minutes after a call completes.
  • Configuration Propagation: Voice changes and talk-time quota modifications synchronize to agents within 10 minutes.

docs.title: Testing & Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide covers local verification workflows, writing automated tests for tools, and containerized production deployment.

docs.title: 1. Local Testing Workflow
docs.text:
Follow this sequence when developing and testing changes:

1. chakra-convai check    ──▶ Validates syntax, prompts, tools, licence
2. chakra-convai prompt   ──▶ Inspects assembled LLM prompt
3. chakra-convai kb       ──▶ Tests knowledge-base retrieval
4. pytest tests/          ──▶ Runs unit tests against skills
5. chakra-convai console  ──▶ Voice conversation via microphone
6. chakra-convai dev      ──▶ Live-reloading server with LiveKit

docs.title: Writing Unit Tests for Skills
docs.text:
Skills inherit from BaseSkill and can be tested directly with pytest using a mock state dictionary:

# tests/test_weather_skill.py
import pytest
from myapp.skills.weather.tool import WeatherSkill

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_weather_skill_returns_clean_fallback(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("OPENWEATHER_API_KEY", raising=False)

    # Provide mock call context
    mock_context = {
        "session_id": "test_session_1",
        "language": "english",
        "caller_number": "0771234567"
    }

    skill = WeatherSkill(mock_context)
    result = await skill.get_current_weather("Kandy")
    assert "STATUS: NOT_CONFIGURED" in result or "Kandy" in result

Run tests from the root of your application repository: 

pytest tests/

docs.title: 2. Production Docker Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy the agent as a container image. The worker only requires outbound network access to LiveKit, Chakra Labs, and Google; it does not listen on inbound public ports.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=fury,env=FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN \
    pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt \
      --extra-index-url "https://${FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN}:@pypi.fury.io/chakra-labs/"

COPY . .
RUN chakra-convai download-files

CMD ["chakra-convai", "start"]

docs.title: Building the Image
docs.text: docker build --secret id=fury,env=FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN -t my-voice-agent .

docs.title: 3. Production Readiness Checklist
docs.text:
• Secrets Management: Supply secrets (CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY, LIVEKIT_*, DATABASE_URL) via environment variables or cloud secret managers. Never hardcode tokens in the Docker image.
  • Agent Name Matching: Set AGENT_NAME to match your LiveKit inbound dispatch SIP rules.
  • Hardware Sizing: Each active concurrent call runs in an isolated process. As a baseline, allocate 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM per worker instance and monitor CPU utilization during peak traffic.
  • Redundancy: Run at least two container replicas to ensure seamless rolling restarts during updates.

docs.title: 4. Production License Behavior
docs.text:
• Startup Validation: The service verifies the license with Chakra Console on startup.
  • Periodic Refresh: The license refreshes in the background every 10 minutes.
  • High-Availability Grace Period: If Chakra Console cannot be contacted due to transient network issues, the worker enters a 6-hour grace period, allowing existing and new calls to proceed uninterrupted.
  • Dynamic Configuration: Changes made in the Console (such as updated talk-time limits or pipeline assignments) apply automatically within 10 minutes without requiring container redeployments.

docs.title: Built-in Features & Database
docs.text: The engine provides built-in tools and call management capabilities out of the box. Enable or disable them via [tools] builtin in chakra.toml.

docs.title: 1. Built-in Tools
docs.text: Built-in tool Parameters What it does save_caller_memory summary, language_preference Stores a short summary of the call against the caller's phone number capture_feedback score (1 to 5) Records caller satisfaction rating query_knowledge_base search_query Searches data/ documents and returns top grounded passages end_call None Says goodbye and hangs up. Requires tools.end_call.description in instructions.json

docs.title: 2. Caller Memory & Greetings
docs.text: When [features] database = true is set and a PostgreSQL database is connected, the engine automatically tracks callers: - Returning Callers: A caller is identified by phone number. If they have called before, the agent greets them using greeting.returning_caller_template, which can reference {last_date}, {base_greeting}, or any stored memory fields. - Memory Fallback: If a call ends abruptly before the model calls save_caller_memory, the engine automatically saves an extractive summary from the caller's spoken turns ([features] memory_fallback = true).

docs.title: 3. Silence Handling
docs.text: When the caller goes quiet, the agent checks in using prompts from [silence] prompts in order. If the caller still does not respond, it speaks [silence] goodbye and ends the call. - monitor mode: Used on the turn-based chakra pipeline. - away mode: Used on Gemini Live (user_away_timeout_seconds, max_check_ins).

docs.title: 4. Maximum Call Length
docs.text: Set [call] max_duration_seconds to cap long calls (e.g., 900 for 15 minutes). The agent speaks the line at max_duration_goodbye and closes the session. Set to 0 for unlimited duration.

docs.title: 5. Daily Talk Time Per Caller
docs.text: Daily talk time limits are configured centrally in Chakra Console and enforced per phone number: 1. When a call connects, the engine sums up the caller's total talk time since midnight in the configured timezone (Asia/Colombo). 2. If less than min_usable_seconds remains, the call is rejected before the greeting with call_limit.limit_reached. 3. If the quota approaches during a call, the caller is warned (call_limit.approaching_limit) and disconnected when time runs out (call_limit.time_up). 4. Daily talk limits reset automatically at midnight.

docs.title: 6. Call Records & PostgreSQL Schema
docs.text:
When DATABASE_URL is configured, the engine maintains the following tables:

Table One row per Main columns call_sessions Call session session_id, phone_number, language, status, duration_seconds, start_time, end_time, handoff_requested, location fields, session_type caller_memory Caller profile phone_number, summary, language_preference, last_interaction_date session_feedback User rating session_id, rating, comment, timestamp conversation_turns Spoken turn Transcripts of each turn with speaker role and timestamp ([features] transcripts = true) knowledge_gaps Unanswered query Questions the agent could not answer, frequency count, and timestamp system_errors Error Unhandled exceptions and system warnings for diagnostic auditing

Data Privacy: This data stays entirely in your own PostgreSQL database. Chakra Labs receives only aggregate call duration, tokens, and billing usage metrics.

docs.title: 7. Distributed Tracing with Langfuse
docs.text:
Set the standard Langfuse environment variables in .env to record end-to-end tracing: - LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY - LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY - LANGFUSE_HOST

Every call generates a trace containing each turn, token usage, latency breakdowns, and tool invocations.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.12 (x86_64 POSIX Linux for production deployment; macOS/Linux/WSL for local dev)
  • License: Active Chakra Console License Key (CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY)
  • LiveKit Server: Self-hosted or LiveKit Cloud URL & API credentials

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
chakra-convai is distributed as a compiled, licensed wheel on Chakra Labs' private Gemfury package index:

pip install chakra-convai --extra-index-url "https://${FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN}:@pypi.fury.io/chakra-labs/"

Security Note: Keep your FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN stored in CI/CD secrets or local environment files (~/.chakra/gemfury.env). Never commit credentials to source control.

docs.title: Scaffolding a New Application: chakra-convai init
docs.text:
The quickest way to bootstrap a new application is with the CLI scaffolding command:

chakra-convai init my-agent-app --channels phone,web_voice,web_chat

If --channels is omitted and CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY is present in your environment, the CLI queries Chakra Console to discover your project's allowed channels automatically.

docs.title: Configuration and Secrets
docs.text:
Copy .env.example to .env and supply your keys:

CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY="your-chakra-license-key"
LIVEKIT_URL="wss://your-project.livekit.cloud"
LIVEKIT_API_KEY="your-livekit-api-key"
LIVEKIT_API_SECRET="your-livekit-api-secret"

# Required only if using gemini_live pipeline or knowledge-base embeddings
GOOGLE_API_KEY="your-google-api-key"

# Optional database for caller memory, daily limits & analytics
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/ivr_db"

docs.title: Running the Application
docs.text: chakra-convai provides built-in commands for every stage of development:

docs.title: 1. Verify Configuration & License
docs.text:
Check that all prompts, tools, pipelines, and license permissions are valid: 

chakra-convai check

docs.title: 2. Interactive Terminal Testing
docs.text:
Talk directly to your agent via audio in your terminal without dialing in or running a full server: 

chakra-convai console

docs.title: 3. Local Development Mode
docs.text:
Run the worker with live code reloading: 

chakra-convai dev

docs.title: 4. Production Worker
docs.text:
Run the LiveKit worker in production: 

chakra-convai start

docs.title: Production Docker Deployment
docs.text:
A complete production Dockerfile requires Python 3.12 and build tools for any native dependencies:

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=fury,env=FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN \
    pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt \
      --extra-index-url "https://${FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN}:@pypi.fury.io/chakra-labs/"

COPY . .

CMD ["chakra-convai", "start"]

Build with buildkit secrets: 

docker build --secret id=fury,env=FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN -t my-chakra-agent .

docs.title: Application Hooks Reference
docs.text:
Application hooks provide extension points to intercept, customize, or override engine behavior without modifying the core SDK.

To register hooks, point to your hooks module in chakra.toml:

[app]
hooks = "myapp.hooks"

All hook functions are optional and can be implemented either synchronously or asynchronously (async def).

docs.title: Hooks Summary Matrix
docs.text: Hook Signature Description resolve_caller(identities: list[str], room_name: str) -> str \| None Extract a carrier-specific caller number (e.g. SIP / IdeaMart MSISDNs) caller_context(shared_state: dict) -> list[str] Extra per-call context lines for the model (season, registered district, etc.) greeting_instruction(shared_state: dict, memory: dict \| None, default: str) -> str Custom greeting instruction (memory is the caller_memory row) admit_caller(shared_state: dict) -> str \| None Gate access before greeting (return None to admit, or prompt string to reject) session_metadata(metadata: dict, shared_state: dict) -> dict \| None Web sessions: read custom application fields from room metadata on_call_start(shared_state: dict) -> None Invoked at session start for custom analytics on_call_end(shared_state: dict, summary: dict) -> None Invoked at session end with token counts, session type, and estimated cost extra_schema() -> list[str] Additive SQL statements run on startup for your own application tables memory_fallback_summary(shared_state: dict, caller_turns: list[str]) -> str \| None The summary stored when the call ends without an explicit save build_system_prompt(instructions: dict, skills: list, language: str, shared_state: dict) -> str Completely overrides the engine's system prompt layout knowledge_chunk(text: str, chunk: dict, shared_state: dict) -> str Rewrite a retrieved knowledge-base passage before the model sees it event_instruction(text: str, kind: str, shared_state: dict) -> str Rewrite lines the agent says for engine events (silence, call limits) tool_result(result: str, name: str, shared_state: dict) -> str Rewrite what a built-in tool returns to the model admin_routers() -> list[APIRouter] Attach custom FastAPI HTTP routes to the admin API

docs.title: 1. admit_caller(shared_state: dict) -> str | None
docs.text:
async def admit_caller(shared_state: dict) -> str | None:
    user = shared_state.get("user_context", {})
    if user.get("is_blocked"):
        return "Your account is currently suspended. Please contact customer support."
    return None

docs.title: 2. caller_context(shared_state: dict) -> list[str]
docs.text:
from datetime import date

def caller_context(shared_state: dict) -> list[str]:
    season = "Maha" if date.today().month in (9, 10, 11, 12, 1, 2) else "Yala"
    district = shared_state.get("district", "Western Province")
    return [
        f"Caller's registered district: {district}",
        f"The current cultivation season is {season}."
    ]

docs.text:
def extra_schema() -> list[str]:
    return [
        """
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS issue_reports (
            id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
            session_id UUID,

        """

docs.title: 4. on_call_end(shared_state: dict, summary: dict) -> None
docs.text:
async def on_call_end(shared_state: dict, summary: dict) -> None:
    # summary carries: session_type, model, input_tokens, cached_tokens, output_tokens, estimated_cost
    logger.info("Call %s ended with estimated cost: $%s", shared_state.get("session_id"), summary.get("estimated_cost"))

docs.title: 5. session_metadata(metadata: dict, shared_state: dict) -> dict | None
docs.text:
def session_metadata(metadata: dict, shared_state: dict) -> dict | None:
    # Extract custom fields sent by web or mobile app
    chakra_data = metadata.get("chakra", {})
    user_context = chakra_data.get("context", {})
    return {"user_tier": user_context.get("tier", "standard")}

docs.title: Knowledge Base (RAG)
docs.text: chakra-convai features an embedded Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system optimized for fast voice interactions without heavy external vector database infrastructure.

docs.title: Document Storage & Formats
docs.text:
Every file under the data/ directory is indexed (subfolders included):

  • Supported Formats: Markdown (.md), Plain Text (.txt), PDF (.pdf), Word (.docx), CSV (.csv), Excel (.xlsx), JSON (.json).
  • Tabular & Structured Data:
  • A CSV or Excel file produces one searchable passage per row.
  • A JSON file holding a list of objects produces one passage per object (using category + content keys).
  • Drafts Convention: Any file or folder whose name starts with an underscore (_) is treated as a draft and is never indexed. Rename it without the leading underscore when you are ready to publish.

docs.title: Building the Index
docs.text:
The vector index is compiled using Google text embeddings and indexed into a local Spotify Annoy index (data/rag.ann) with metadata store (data/rag.json).

Generate or update the vector index locally before deployment:

chakra-convai build-rag

To clear existing indices and rebuild completely from scratch:

chakra-convai build-rag --clean

Test retrieval directly from your terminal:

chakra-convai kb "How do I identify fall armyworm?" sinhala

docs.title: Tool Configuration in Prompts
docs.text:
The built-in tool query_knowledge_base is automatically enabled when declared in chakra.toml:

[tools]
builtin = ["query_knowledge_base"]

The phrasing the model receives with retrieved results is configured in config/instructions.json under: - tools.query_knowledge_base.found_directive - tools.query_knowledge_base.not_found_directive

docs.title: Admin API & S3 Mirroring
docs.text:
chakra-convai admin-api starts a lightweight HTTP document management service on port 8080:

Method and Path Purpose POST /upload Upload a new document into data/ GET /files List all current documents in data/ DELETE /files/{filename} Delete a document POST /trigger_rebuild Trigger a background vector index rebuild GET /status, GET /status/{job_id} Check progress and status of a rebuild job

docs.title: Distributed Deployments (S3)
docs.text:
If RAG_S3_BUCKET is configured in .env: 

RAG_S3_BUCKET="my-org-rag-artifacts"
RAG_S3_PREFIX="rag"  # Optional prefix, default: rag
The Admin API automatically publishes uploads and rebuilt indices to S3. Running voice agent worker containers download the updated index without requiring a code redeployment or container restart.

docs.title: Licensing & Quotas
docs.text: chakra-convai requires a valid license issued by Chakra Console (CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY). The engine will refuse to start or serve calls without a verified license.

docs.title: Cryptographic License Verification
docs.text:
1. Startup Check: On boot, the engine contacts Chakra Console's /v2/verify endpoint.
  2. Cryptographic Signature: The license payload is signed using Ed25519; the engine verifies this signature against Chakra Labs' public key.
  3. Periodic Recheck: During execution, the license is periodically refreshed.
  4. Grace Period: If the network connection to Chakra Console experiences a transient outage, the engine enters a configurable grace period, ensuring ongoing phone calls and web sessions are not interrupted.

docs.title: Governed Attributes
docs.text: Chakra Console centrally governs several core operational constraints:

docs.title: 1. Project Type & Channel Entitlements
docs.text:
A project license authorizes specific channel combinations: - phone - web_voice - web_chat

If an application attempts to launch a session on an unauthorized channel, the session is refused with caller_refused.

docs.title: 2. Pipeline Allocations & Pins
docs.text: The license dictates which speech pipelines (chakra managed, gemini_live) the application can use, and may optionally pin specific agents to dedicated pipelines.

docs.title: 3. Daily Talk Time Limit Per Caller
docs.text:
To prevent runaway billing or spam callers, Chakra Console configures the maximum daily talk time allowed per unique telephone number.

The engine tracks cumulative call minutes in PostgreSQL. When a caller approaches their daily quota, warning prompts ([call_limit] approaching_limit) play before the call politely concludes ([call_limit] time_up).

docs.title: Usage Reporting
docs.text: At the end of each session, chakra-convai securely reports usage metrics to Chakra Console: - Session Type (phone, web_voice, web_chat) - Model utilized - Cumulative token usage (text tokens, speech input/output audio seconds, vision frames) - Session duration

docs.title: Speech & Multimodal Pipelines
docs.text: chakra-convai features a dual-pipeline architecture. Chakra Console assigns which pipelines a license is entitled to execute, with agent-level overrides governed remotely.

docs.title: 1. Managed chakra Pipeline
docs.text:
The chakra pipeline is Chakra Labs' fully managed, turn-based voice stack:

User Audio
    │
    ▼
[Silero VAD] (Local Voice Activity Detection)
    │
    ▼
[Chakra STT] (Speech-to-Text on Chakra GPU Fleet)
    │
    ▼
[Managed LLM] (High-throughput OpenAI-compatible route on Fleet)
    │
    ▼
[Chakra TTS] (Natural low-latency Text-to-Speech synthesis)
    │
    ▼
Caller Audio Stream

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Zero Provider Configuration: Clients configure no model names, no external LLM API keys, and no TTS audio hyper-parameters. Everything routes securely through the Chakra Gateway authenticated by CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY.
  • Fleet Optimization: Speech models and LLM engines are continuously tuned and upgraded on Chakra GPU clusters without client application redeployments.
  • Vision Support: In web voice sessions, camera frames are packaged alongside speech transcripts to the fleet vision model.

docs.title: 2. Realtime gemini_live Pipeline
docs.text:
The gemini_live pipeline leverages Google's Gemini Live realtime multimodal WebSocket streaming:

User Audio & Video
    │
    ▼
[LiveKit Audio/Video Tracks]
    │
    ▼
[Google Gemini Live Session] (Bidirectional streaming)
    │
    ▼
Synthesized Audio Return

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Bidirectional Streaming: Ultra-low latency voice-to-voice streaming with natural barge-in interruptions.
  • Native Video Track Ingestion: Streams camera and screen sharing directly to the Gemini Live multimodal model.
  • Requirements: Requires a valid GOOGLE_API_KEY set in your .env.

docs.title: Language Enforcer & Policy
docs.text:
• Dynamic Language Detection: If an agent is not pinned to a specific language, the call language dynamically tracks the caller's spoken language based on turn transcript analysis (Sinhala, Tamil, or English).
  • Pinned Language Enforcement: When pinned to a single language (e.g. language = "si"), chakra-convai injects the language enforcement patch (language_policy.forced_enforcer_default) to ensure Gemini does not drift across languages during interruptions.

docs.title: Pipeline Governance & Precedence
docs.text:
1. Chakra Console Assignment: The signed response from /v2/verify lists the authorized pipelines and per-agent pins.
  2. Environment Variable: CHAKRA_PIPELINE can select between authorized pipelines.
  3. Application Setting: [pipeline] type in chakra.toml specifies the application's default choice among licensed pipelines.

If an application requests a pipeline not permitted by the license, chakra-convai logs a warning and falls back to the license's default pipeline.

Run chakra-convai check to view the resolved pipeline for each configured agent.

docs.title: Prompts & instructions.json
docs.text: Everything the model is told comes from config/instructions.json. The engine assembles the system prompt from it on every call, so changing agent behavior means editing this file, not Python code.

docs.title: Structure of config/instructions.json
docs.text: Key Required What it holds agent_profile Yes name, description, supported_languages, and persona with its voice_guidelines list system_directives.core_rules Yes The list of rules the agent always follows conversation_states_and_flows Yes The stages of a call: opening, working out what the caller wants, handling it, closing guardrails_and_fallbacks Yes What to do when a tool fails, a question is out of scope, or language is unsupported system_guardrails No identity_anchor, immutable_rules, boundary_enforcement, anti_extraction, tool_safety tools.<name>.description For built-ins Descriptions of built-in tools. end_call must have one languages.<lang>.prompts Yes Per-language lines: assistant, greeting, returning_greeting, silence_reprompt, silence_disconnect greeting.returning_caller_template If used How a returning caller is greeted language_policy Gemini Live The per-reply language reminder (forced_enforcer_default, forced_enforcer_suffix) agent_profile.terminology_glossary No Domain terms and phonetic spellings the agent should use

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
{
  "agent_profile": {
    "name": "My Helpline",
    "description": "A phone assistant for agriculture",
    "supported_languages": ["sinhala", "english"],
    "persona": {
      "role": "A friendly, patient advisor",
      "voice_guidelines": [
        "Keep answers short: this is a phone call.",
        "Ask one question at a time."
      ]
    }
  },
  "system_directives": {
    "core_rules": [
      "Never invent facts. Use a tool or say you do not know."
    ]
  },
  "conversation_states_and_flows": {
    "1_initiation": "Greet the caller and ask how you can help.",
    "2_intent_execution": "Use the right tool, then answer briefly.",
    "3_closing": "Ask for a 1 to 5 rating, save a summary, then end the call."
  },
  "guardrails_and_fallbacks": {
    "api_failure_fallback": "Apologise briefly and say there is a system issue.",
    "out_of_scope_queries": "Politely say you can only help with agriculture."
  },
  "tools": {
    "end_call": {
      "description": "End the call after the caller says goodbye."
    }
  },
  "languages": {
    "english": {
      "prompts": {
        "assistant": "Speak plain, warm English.",
        "greeting": "Greet the caller and introduce the service.",
        "silence_reprompt": "Ask if the caller is still there.",
        "silence_disconnect": "Say goodbye and that you are ending the call."
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Per-Skill Prompt Files
docs.text:
Each skill can maintain its own prompt advice and flows in config/modules/<skill>/prompts.json, loaded cleanly using PromptLoader:

{
  "instructions": {
    "get_current_weather": {
      "when_to_use": "When the caller asks about the weather or rainfall."
    }
  },
  "flows": {
    "WEATHER_INQUIRY": {
      "agent_instruction": "Handle weather and farming condition queries."
    }
  }
}

Load it inside your skill: 

from chakra_convai import PromptLoader

cfg = PromptLoader.load("weather")

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• State each rule once: The entire prompt is sent with every turn. Repetition increases token latency and costs without improving adherence.
  • Write Sinhala and Tamil in native script: Write lines in the spoken style you want. A model told in English to "speak Sinhala" tends to sound stiff, overly formal, and literary.
  • Do not repeat tool descriptions in the prompt: The model automatically receives @function_tool descriptions attached to tool declarations.
  • Inspect assembled prompts: Run chakra-convai prompt <language> to review the exact prompt the model sees at runtime.

docs.title: Building Skills & Tools
docs.text:
Skills are how your application exposes custom tools and business logic to the LLM.

All skills placed in the directory pointed to by [app] skills in chakra.toml (e.g. myapp.skills) are automatically discovered and loaded when the engine boots.

docs.title: Skill Architecture
docs.text:
A skill is a Python package containing a subclass of BaseSkill and exposing methods decorated with @function_tool.

myapp/
└── skills/
    └── weather/
        ├── __init__.py
        └── tool.py          # Implements BaseSkill

docs.title: Writing a Skill
docs.text:
Here is a complete example of a skill that fetches localized agricultural weather data:

# myapp/skills/weather/tool.py
from typing import Annotated
from chakra_convai import BaseSkill, function_tool, tool_description, logger, get_db_pool

class WeatherSkill(BaseSkill):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.logger = logger.getChild("skills.weather")

    @function_tool(description=tool_description("get_weather"))
    async def get_weather(
        self,
        district: Annotated[str, "The Sri Lankan administrative district (e.g., Kandy, Anuradhapura)"],
    ) -> str:
        """Fetches the 24-hour agricultural weather forecast for a given district."""
        self.logger.info("Fetching forecast for district: %s", district)

        # Access the application's PostgreSQL connection pool
        pool = get_db_pool()
        if pool:
            async with pool.acquire() as conn:
                record = await conn.fetchrow(
                    "SELECT forecast, rainfall_mm FROM weather_cache WHERE district = $1",
                    district
                )
                if record:
                    return f"Forecast for {district}: {record['forecast']} with {record['rainfall_mm']}mm expected rain."

        return f"Normal seasonal conditions reported across {district}."

docs.title: @function_tool
docs.text: The standard LiveKit tool decorator. Decorates async or sync methods to expose them to the model.

docs.title: tool_description(tool_name: str)
docs.text: Extracts the tool description directly from config/instructions.json using the active session language. This ensures the model receives tool descriptions in the caller's target language without hardcoding prompts in Python.

docs.title: get_db_pool()
docs.text: Retrieves the active asyncpg PostgreSQL connection pool initialized by the engine. You can use this pool to query your own application-specific database tables.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Use logger from chakra_convai to write formatted, tracing-aware log messages.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: This section covers common issues, root causes, and recommended solutions when developing or running applications on chakra-convai.

docs.title: Diagnostic Matrix
docs.text: Symptom Likely Cause Recommended Resolution pip cannot find chakra-convai The install token is missing or invalid, or the system is not Linux x86_64 with Python 3.12 Verify FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN is set in the environment. On Windows or macOS, build and run inside Docker or WSL. Install fails while building annoy Missing C++ compiler toolchain Use the full python:3.12 base image or install g++ (apt-get install -y build-essential). "Chakra Console licence check failed" at start CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY is missing, suspended, or outbound network access is blocked Check your key in .env. Run chakra-convai licence to inspect status. Contact Chakra Labs if suspended. chakra-convai check reports a missing instruction key A required key is missing or empty in config/instructions.json Review the error output from chakra-convai check and add the missing keys. A skill's tools are missing The skill failed to import, or the directory lacks __init__.py or tool.py Run chakra-convai check to view the import traceback. The agent never answers incoming calls AGENT_NAME does not match the LiveKit dispatch rule, or LiveKit credentials are wrong Ensure [[agents]] name in chakra.toml matches your SIP dispatch rule in LiveKit Cloud. A different pipeline runs than configured The license does not permit the requested pipeline Run chakra-convai check to view allowed pipelines. Request pipeline additions in Chakra Console. The agent is silent on Chakra Voice The response is in a language not supported by Chakra Voice Chakra Voice speaks Sinhala. For Tamil or English voice sessions, use the gemini_live pipeline. A Console update has no effect The periodic sync cycle has not elapsed Wait up to 10 minutes for running workers to synchronize with Chakra Console. No redeploy is needed. Daily talk-time limits are ignored DATABASE_URL is unset, or caller identity is anonymous Verify PostgreSQL connectivity ([features] database = true). Ensure caller ID is detected. Returning callers are not recognized Caller memory is unconfigured or was never saved on the previous call Verify save_caller_memory is in [tools] builtin and database connectivity is operational. Knowledge base queries return empty results Documents are marked as drafts (name starts with _), index not built, or GOOGLE_API_KEY missing Rename drafts, verify GOOGLE_API_KEY, and run chakra-convai build-rag. Uploaded voice shows "Could not be used" Audio file is not 5–10 seconds, is silent, or does not match transcript text Upload a clean, noise-free .wav clip and ensure transcript words match the spoken audio exactly.

docs.title: Contacting Support & Reporting Issues
docs.text:
When requesting assistance from Chakra Labs support: 1. Provide the output of: 

chakra-convai version
chakra-convai check
2. Include the timestamp of the affected call, along with the session_id and error logs. 3. Security Caution: Never share your CHAKRA_LICENSE_KEY or FURY_DEPLOY_TOKEN in support chats, tickets, or public issue trackers.

docs.title: Chakra Console — Overview
docs.text: Chakra Console (chakra-ivr-admin) is the management plane that sits alongside the chakra-convai engine. It gives Chakra Labs the tools to provision customers, issue and rotate licence keys, inspect GPU-fleet health, and see per-project usage analytics — all from a single web dashboard.

docs.title: Two components, one database
docs.text:
Component What it is chakra-license-hub/ Chakra Console — Next.js 16 admin dashboard. Handles dashboard analytics, organisations, projects, licence keys, packages, voice settings, and GPU fleet. chakra-license-server/ License Server — FastAPI microservice. Exposes the signed /v2/verify endpoint consumed by every chakra-convai instance and /track-usage for usage metering.

Both services connect to the same PostgreSQL (Neon) admin database, so a key created in the dashboard is active at the speech gateway within seconds.

Chakra Console (Next.js)
       │ CRUD
       ▼
  PostgreSQL (Neon)   ◄─── License Server (FastAPI)
       │                         │
       │                         ├─ /v2/verify   ◄── chakra-convai (startup check)
       │                         ├─ /v2/gemini-token ◄── Gemini Live sessions
       │                         └─ /track-usage ◄── chakra-convai (after each call)

docs.title: Role model
docs.text: Role Who Can do Chakra Labs Admin ADMIN_USERS env var Create/edit organisations, projects, packages, licence keys, console users Organisation user Per-organisation sign-in View own projects' dashboards, change daily talk-time, voice, and own password

docs.title: Database & Migrations
docs.text: Both chakra-license-hub and chakra-license-server share a single PostgreSQL database (Neon managed Postgres in production).

docs.title: licenses
docs.text:
The primary table. One row per project.

Column Type Description id serial Primary key name text Project display name company text Customer company (legacy; now superseded by organizations) token_hash text SHA-256 of the licence key token_prefix text First 16 chars (display only) is_active boolean Whether the licence accepts sessions package text Service tier (must match packages.yaml) channels text Comma-separated channel list pipelines text Comma-separated pipeline list used_minutes integer Cumulative minutes across all calls daily_limit_seconds integer Per-caller daily cap limit_warning_seconds integer Warning threshold gemini_voice text Voice name for Gemini Live greeting_mode text recorded / auto / empty greeting_id text ID of the uploaded greeting clip greeting_text text Transcript of the greeting google_access text gateway or empty gemini_api_key_enc bytea Encrypted Gemini API key (NaCl secretbox)

docs.title: organizations
docs.text: Column Type Description id serial Primary key name text Organisation display name package text Package applied to all projects email text Organisation user login password_hash text scrypt hash

docs.title: call_usage
docs.text: Hourly voice call metrics. Composite unique key on (license_id, hour, pipeline).

docs.title: chat_usage
docs.text: Hourly chat metrics. Composite unique key on (license_id, hour).

docs.title: Running migrations
docs.text:
Migrations live in chakra-license-server/migrations/. They are plain SQL files applied in numeric order.

cd chakra-license-server
python init_db.py   # creates all tables and applies migration 001 automatically

docs.title: Migration 001 — Hash tokens
docs.text:
001_hash_tokens.sql — Additive and safe to run on a live database.

  • Adds token_hash and token_prefix columns to licenses.
  • Hashes every existing plaintext key into token_hash.
  • Existing client keys continue to work (the server falls back to plaintext during the transition).

docs.title: Migration 002 — Drop plaintext tokens
docs.text:
002_drop_plaintext_tokens.sql — Irreversible. Run only after all services are updated.

  • Drops the token (plaintext) column from licenses.
  • After this, no plaintext key can ever be read back.

Irreversible

Run migration 002 only after:

  1. The new license server and hub are deployed and verified.
  2. All running chakra-convai instances have been restarted with their new (hashed-lookup compatible) keys.

docs.title: One-time steps for the existing database
docs.text:
Required for security

These steps address a historical credential leak where DATABASE_URL was committed to the repository.

  1. Rotate the Neon database password. The old password is in git history and must be treated as public. After rotating, update DATABASE_URL in:

    • chakra-license-server/.env
    • chakra-license-hub/.env.local
    • chakra-gpu-fleet environment

  2. Apply migration 001 (run python init_db.py or execute the SQL directly). This adds the hash columns and populates them. Additive — safe on a live database.

  3. Deploy the new admin hub, license server, and speech gateway.

  4. Apply migration 002 (once all deployments are verified). Drops the plaintext token column.

docs.title: Local development database
docs.text:
# Start a local Postgres instance (Docker)
docker run -d -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=dev postgres:16

# Set DATABASE_URL
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:dev@localhost:5432/chakra_admin

# Initialise
python chakra-license-server/init_db.py

docs.title: GPU Fleet
docs.text: The GPU Fleet section of Chakra Console gives Chakra Labs engineers a live view of every GPU node running chakra-convai workloads.

docs.title: Fleet overview
docs.text:
The fleet dashboard aggregates health metrics collected by chakra-gpu-fleet and presents them per node and per package tier:

Metric Description Node status Online / offline / degraded GPU utilisation Current % of GPU compute used Active sessions Live voice and chat sessions per node Errors / restarts Crash count and last restart time Package allocation Which packages are assigned to which nodes

docs.title: Fleet health status
docs.text:
The fleet-health.ts library polls the fleet control host (via FLEET_* environment variables) and aggregates:

  • healthy — node is reachable and processing sessions.
  • degraded — node is reachable but reporting errors or high utilisation.
  • offline — node has not responded within the health-check window.

docs.title: GPU page
docs.text:
The GPU tab inside Fleet shows per-GPU metrics:

  • VRAM used / total
  • Thermal readings (where available)
  • Model loaded (e.g., which Whisper or TTS checkpoint)
  • Inference latency (p50, p95)

docs.title: Fleet context
docs.text: The fleet-context.tsx and hub-context.tsx React contexts share the fleet and hub state across all pages in the dashboard, so node counts and health indicators update in real time without a full page reload.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Fleet endpoints and credentials are set via environment variables in chakra-license-hub/.env.local:

FLEET_HOST=https://fleet.internal.chakralabs.lk
FLEET_API_KEY=your_fleet_api_key

These values are never exposed to the browser; all fleet calls go through the Next.js API routes (/api/fleet).

docs.title: License Server API
docs.text:
chakra-license-server is a FastAPI microservice that is the authoritative licence gate for all chakra-convai deployments. Every engine call goes through it.

Base URL (production): https://license.chakralabs.lk (behind Caddy on the fleet control host).

docs.title: POST /v2/verify
docs.text: Verifies a licence key and returns a signed JWT-style payload the engine stores for the session duration.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
{
  "token": "ck_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "nonce": "random-string-per-call"
}
Field Type Description token string Plaintext licence key nonce string Random value to prevent replay

docs.title: Response 200 OK
docs.text:
{
  "payload": "<base64-encoded JSON>",
  "signature": "<base64 Ed25519 signature>"
}

The decoded payload contains:

{
  "license_id": 42,
  "is_active": true,
  "package": "National Plus",
  "channels": ["phone", "web_voice"],
  "pipelines": ["gemini_live", "chakra_voice"],
  "daily_limit_seconds": 3600,
  "limit_warning_seconds": 300,
  "gemini_voice": "Aoede",
  "greeting_mode": "recorded",
  "greeting_id": "greet_abc123",
  "greeting_text": "Welcome to Acme support.",
  "google_access": "gateway",
  "key_hash": "sha256:...",
  "nonce": "random-string-per-call",
  "issued_at": 1728900000
}

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text: Code Meaning 403 Key not found, inactive, or channel mismatch 503 Database unavailable

docs.title: POST /v2/gemini-token
docs.text: Issues a one-session Gemini Live ephemeral token for projects where google_access = gateway (the project holds no Google API key).

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
{
  "token": "ck_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "nonce": "per-session-nonce",
  "agent": "optional-agent-label"
}

docs.title: Response 200 OK
docs.text:
{
  "token": "auth_tokens/...",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-16T18:00:00Z",
  "api_version": "v1alpha"
}

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text: Up to 120 tokens per licence per minute. A single session renewal counts as one token. Exceeds 429.

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text: Code Meaning 403 Inactive licence 409 Project uses its own key / no Gemini key stored / Gemini Live not in pipeline 429 Rate limit exceeded 502 Google refused to issue token

docs.title: POST /track-usage
docs.text: Records a finished session against the licence. Called by chakra-convai after every call or chat.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
{
  "token": "ck_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "seconds": 142.5,
  "pipeline": "gemini_live",
  "session_type": "phone"
}
Field Type Options session_type string phone, web_voice, web_chat pipeline string gemini_live, chakra_voice, twilio_voice, unknown seconds float Duration of the session in seconds tokens object {input, cached, output} — for web_chat only

docs.title: Response 200 OK
docs.text:
{
  "status": "updated",
  "total_minutes": 1234
}

Web chat sessions return "status": "updated" with "session_type": "web_chat" instead of total_minutes.

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
cd chakra-license-server
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env    # fill DATABASE_URL and SIGNING_KEY
python init_db.py       # creates tables, applies migration 001
uvicorn main:app --port 8000 --reload

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Description DATABASE_URL PostgreSQL connection string (Neon or local) SIGNING_KEY Ed25519 private key (base64) for payload signing GEMINI_TOKEN_MOCK Set to 1 in tests to skip real Google calls

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker build -t chakra-license-server .
docker run -p 8000:8000 --env-file .env chakra-license-server

In production it runs behind Caddy on the fleet control host alongside chakra-license-hub.

docs.title: License Management
docs.text: Licences are the unit of deployment for chakra-convai. Each project has exactly one licence key that the engine presents on startup and after every call.

docs.title: Licence key lifecycle
docs.text:
Created (key shown once)
       │
       ▼
  Active ──────────────────────────────────────┐
       │                                       │
  Rotate key (old key expires within 60 s)     │
       │                                       │
  New key shown once ──────────────────────────┘
       │
  Deactivate (is_active = false)
       │
  No sessions accepted

Keys are shown once only

When a licence key is created or rotated, the plaintext is displayed once. After that only the first 16 characters are visible. Store it in a secrets manager immediately.

docs.title: Licence fields
docs.text: Field Type Notes key / token_hash SHA-256 of the plaintext key Never stored in plaintext after migration 002 token_prefix First 16 characters Shown in the dashboard for identification is_active boolean Deactivated licences are rejected at /v2/verify channels phone, web_voice, web_chat (comma list) Signed into JWT payload; mismatch = 403 used_minutes integer Incremented by /track-usage after each call daily_limit_seconds integer Per-caller daily cap (0 = none) limit_warning_seconds integer Seconds remaining when a warning is sent

docs.title: Rotating a key
docs.text:
1. Open the project in the dashboard.
  2. Click Rotate key.
  3. The new plaintext key is shown once — copy it now.
  4. The old key remains valid for up to 60 seconds to allow in-flight sessions to finish, then becomes invalid.
  5. Deploy the new key to all running chakra-convai instances (restart or environment update).

docs.title: Deactivating a licence
docs.text:
• Toggle Active off on the project card.
  • The license server rejects /v2/verify immediately.
  • Ongoing calls are not disconnected mid-session, but no new sessions start.

docs.title: Usage tracking
docs.text: chakra-convai posts to /track-usage at the end of every call. Usage is accumulated per hour in two tables:

docs.title: call_usage (phone & web voice)
docs.text: Column Description license_id FK to licenses hour date_trunc('hour', now()) pipeline gemini_live, chakra_voice, etc. calls Number of calls in that hour call_seconds Total audio seconds web_calls / web_seconds Web-voice subset

docs.title: chat_usage (web chat)
docs.text: Column Description license_id FK to licenses hour Bucket chats Number of chat sessions chat_seconds Total chat duration input_tokens / cached_tokens / output_tokens LLM token breakdown

docs.title: Licences page
docs.text: The Licences page in the dashboard shows all active and inactive licences across all organisations, with search, filter by status, and a quick link to the parent project. Admins can create a standalone licence here or navigate to an organisation project.

docs.title: Organizations & Projects
docs.text: Chakra Console organises customers in a two-level hierarchy: organisations own one or more projects.

docs.title: Organisations
docs.text:
An organisation represents a customer company. It holds:

  • A single package that applies to every project under it.
  • One Chakra Console sign-in — the organisation user can see all its own projects and nothing else.

Only Chakra Labs admins (listed in ADMIN_USERS) can create or edit organisations.

docs.title: Creating an organisation
docs.text:
1. Open Organizations in the left sidebar.
  2. Click New Organization.
  3. Enter the company name, contact email, and assign a package.
  4. A sign-in credential (email + password) is created for the organisation user. Share it securely.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
A project is one conversational AI deployment. It maps 1-to-1 with a row in the licenses table and has its own licence key.

Each project carries:

Field Description Licence key Unique token authenticated by the license server. Shown once; stored as a SHA-256 hash. Project type (channels) phone, web_voice, web_chat — any combination. Signed into the licence payload; chakra-convai 0.8+ rejects sessions on unlisted channels. Empty = all channels allowed. Voice pipeline e.g. gemini_live, chakra_voice, twilio_voice. Voice Gemini voice name for gemini_live pipelines (blank = app decides). Greeting mode recorded plays a pre-uploaded audio clip; auto generates a greeting; blank = app handles it. Daily talk time Per-caller limit in seconds (0 = unlimited). chakra-convai 0.5+ enforces it. Google access gateway = project holds no Google key; Gemini Live sessions must call /v2/gemini-token.

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the parent Organization → Projects tab.
  2. Click New Project.
  3. Configure the project type, pipeline, and voice.
  4. Copy the licence key shown on creation — it cannot be retrieved later.

docs.title: Editing a project
docs.text: All fields except the licence key are editable. Changes take effect at the next chakra-convai startup (or key re-verification).

docs.title: Project type card
docs.text:
When you open a project, the Project Type card shows the exact CLI flags needed to match your channel selection:

# Phone-only project
chakra-convai init --channels phone

# Multi-channel: phone + web voice
chakra-convai init --channels phone,web_voice

# Web chat only
chakra-convai init --channels web_chat

docs.title: Migration from pre-organisation licences
docs.text:
Before 2026-10-12, each licence stood alone with its own package and sign-in. On first hub load after the upgrade, the hub automatically:

  1. Groups licences by company name into organisations.
  2. Creates one organisation sign-in per company (the old per-licence credential is promoted).
  3. Assigns the licence's existing package to the organisation.

Existing credentials continue to work without any action needed.

docs.title: Packages & Billing
docs.text: A package defines the service tier for an organisation. Every project under that organisation inherits the same package.

docs.title: Package names
docs.text:
Package names must match the entries in chakra-gpu-fleet/fleet/packages.yaml, which the fleet manager uses to size GPU capacity.

Package name Tier Essential Entry-level Essential Plus Entry-level+ National Mid-range National Plus Mid-range+ Enterprise Full capacity

Legacy names

Licences created under the old naming scheme (Starter, Growth, Scale, Enterprise MD/LG) are automatically remapped by the fleet manager. No dashboard action needed.

docs.title: Setting an organisation's package
docs.text:
1. Open Organizations → select the organisation.
  2. Click Edit on the package card.
  3. Choose the new package from the dropdown.
  4. Save — the change applies to every project under the organisation immediately.

The GPU fleet reads these values to reserve capacity. Changing a package mid-billing period may affect fleet resource allocation within minutes.

docs.title: Package enforcement in chakra-convai
docs.text:
The licence verification response includes the package name. chakra-convai uses it to:

  • Enforce concurrent-session limits (defined per package in packages.yaml).
  • Apply talk-time limits appropriate for the tier.
  • Gate access to premium pipelines (e.g., chakra_voice requires National+).

docs.title: Packages page
docs.text: The Packages page lists every package currently assigned, how many organisations hold it, and the total active licences under each package tier. Use it to plan capacity ahead of tier changes.

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: Chakra Console is designed with defence in depth: every layer independently validates identity, and secrets never leave the server.

docs.title: Session cookies
docs.text:
• Sessions are HMAC-signed, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookies with a 12-hour TTL.
  • src/proxy.ts intercepts every request before it reaches Next.js routes — anyone without a valid session is redirected to /login.
  • Every API route (/api/**) re-validates the session server-side before touching any data. A stolen (or replayed) cookie from another origin cannot be used.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text:
• 10 failed sign-in attempts per IP triggers a 15-minute lockout.
  • The lockout is in-memory (process-scoped); a server restart resets it. For production, back it with Redis if multiple hub replicas are deployed.

docs.title: Admin users
docs.text:
Admins are defined entirely in the server environment, not in the database:

# .env.local
ADMIN_USERS=alice@chakralabs.lk=<scrypt-hash> bob@chakralabs.lk=<scrypt-hash>

Generate a hash:

cd chakra-license-hub
pnpm hash-password alice@chakralabs.lk
# prints: alice@chakralabs.lk=<hash>  — paste into ADMIN_USERS

Removing an entry takes effect on the next request — no database change, no restart required.

docs.title: Licence key hashing
docs.text:
Step Detail Creation Plaintext key is generated server-side (CSPRNG). Shown once Plaintext is returned to the admin in the creation response only. Stored token_hash = SHA-256(plaintext). token_prefix = first 16 characters. Verified License server hashes the incoming token and does WHERE token_hash = $1. After migration 002 token (plaintext) column is dropped permanently. Keys can never be read back.

Lost key = rotate, not recover

There is no way to recover a lost key. Use Rotate key to invalidate the old one and issue a new one.

docs.title: Gemini API key encryption
docs.text:
Projects that use google_access = gateway store a Gemini API key in the database. It is encrypted at rest using the secret_box.py module (NaCl secretbox / XSalsa20-Poly1305):

SECRET_KEY=<32-byte base64 key>   # in license-server .env

The key is decrypted only in-memory when minting a Gemini Live token, and never logged or returned to the client.

docs.title: Cross-site request protection
docs.text:
• SameSite=Strict cookies prevent CSRF on all modern browsers.
  • All state-changing API routes additionally validate the session token from the cookie directly — there are no CSRF tokens to manage separately.

docs.title: No secrets in the repository
docs.text:
• .env and .env.local files are in .gitignore.
  • .env.example files show required variable names with placeholder values.
  • The historical credential leak (hard-coded DATABASE_URL in early init_db.py) has been remediated — see Database & Migrations → One-time steps.

docs.title: Setup & Deployment
docs.text: Complete guide to running Chakra Console locally and deploying it to production.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Requirement Version Node.js 20+ pnpm 10 (via corepack) Python 3.11+ PostgreSQL 15+ (or Neon serverless) Docker 24+ (optional, for production)

docs.title: 1. Admin hub (Next.js)
docs.text:
cd chakra-license-hub

# Install dependencies (corepack ensures pnpm 10)
corepack enable
pnpm install

# Configure environment
cp .env.example .env.local

Edit .env.local:

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host/dbname
SESSION_SECRET=at-least-32-random-characters
ADMIN_USERS=you@chakralabs.lk=<scrypt-hash>
FLEET_HOST=https://fleet.internal.chakralabs.lk
FLEET_API_KEY=your-fleet-api-key

Generate an admin password hash:

pnpm hash-password you@chakralabs.lk
# Output: you@chakralabs.lk=<hash>   ← paste into ADMIN_USERS

Start the dev server:

pnpm dev
# → http://localhost:3000

docs.title: 2. License server (FastAPI)
docs.text:
cd chakra-license-server

pip install -r requirements.txt

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env:

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host/dbname
SIGNING_KEY=<base64-encoded Ed25519 private key>
SECRET_KEY=<32-byte base64 NaCl secretbox key>

Initialise the database and apply migration 001:

python init_db.py

Start the server:

uvicorn main:app --port 8000 --reload
# → http://localhost:8000

docs.title: Production deployment (Docker + Caddy)
docs.text: Both services run on the fleet control host behind Caddy as a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Build images
docs.text:
# Admin hub
cd chakra-license-hub
docker build -t chakra-license-hub:latest .

# License server
cd chakra-license-server
docker build -t chakra-license-server:latest .

docs.title: Run containers
docs.text:
docker run -d \
  --name license-hub \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  --env-file .env.local \
  chakra-license-hub:latest

docker run -d \
  --name license-server \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  --env-file .env \
  chakra-license-server:latest

docs.title: Caddy configuration (example)
docs.text:
console.chakralabs.lk {
    reverse_proxy localhost:3000
}

license.chakralabs.lk {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8000
}

Caddy handles TLS automatically via Let's Encrypt.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text: Endpoint Service Expected GET / License hub Redirects to /login (302) GET /api/auth License hub {"authenticated": false} GET /health License server {"status": "ok"} POST /v2/verify License server 403 with invalid token (server is reachable)

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
# Pull latest
git -C chakra-ivr-admin pull

# Rebuild and restart (production)
docker build -t chakra-license-hub:latest chakra-license-hub/
docker build -t chakra-license-server:latest chakra-license-server/
docker restart license-hub license-server

Zero-downtime restarts

The license server is stateless (no in-memory session state beyond rate limiting). You can restart it without dropping active calls — chakra-convai retries /v2/verify on connection failure.
